title: Rendering options for clouds and storms on a globe
status: research only; nothing ships; no payload, desktop, docs or repo file changed
bottom_line: Phase 1: (a) draped GOES imagery first; (g) NWS radar drape as fallback.
Phase 2: (b) cloud deck lifted by height. ACHA2KMC 2 km ranks first on footprint (4.9 x 2.2 km vs 24 x 11 km), gated on a DQF-0 count not yet measured; ACHAC 10 km ranks second on server bytes.
Phase 3: (d) sparse boxes at 50 then 35 dBZ first; (e) isosurfaces after d, with an interpolation caveat; (c) ray-marching only as a measured experiment; (f) as a level inspector only.

No browser-based GOES or NEXRAD 3D volume viewer was found in nine searches. Verified survey entries: desktop or native (ArcGIS Pro, Unreal Engine, a GPU research system) and one flat-map globe (Windy).
No GPU timing exists: every WebGL number is SwiftShader in headless Chromium 141. GPU classes are reasoned from counts and sizes.
constraints_checked: Python computes data, time, geometry, thresholds and freshness; the browser draws (D1, rule 4). One fixed Montana + border product, never a place list (D-G3). No paid token or Google tiles (D-G4). Any 3D view ships behind a default-off setting. Cesium viewer defaults call Ion, so Cesium options set baseLayer explicitly.
box: Montana + border = prototype DEFAULT_BBOX lon -116.8..-103.3, lat 43.6..49.75 (mrms_volume.py; GOES grid 43.59..49.75 in prototype-goes.json). MRMS 1350 x 615 = 830,250 cells per level; 33 levels = 27,398,250 cells (computed). Review box lon -116.05..-104.04, lat 44.36..49.00 (goes-aws.json) is cited only where its source uses it.

measured_inputs.voxels_event_peak: 2025-06-15T23:12:41Z, 33 levels, default box (prototype-mrms.json; out-v2 files): >=20 dBZ 619,321 voxels, 10,327,224 B; >=35 dBZ 99,854 voxels, 1,666,106 B; >=50 dBZ 13,482 voxels, 232,822 B. Sample peak, not a day maximum.
measured_inputs.voxels_quiet: 2026-10-17T03:04:41Z, 33 levels: 0 voxels at 20 and 35 dBZ; JSON 9,642 B (prototype-mrms.json run R3).

inputs_read: README sections 1-7; supervisor-log; DECISIONS D1, D2, D4, D7-D9, D12, D19, D23, D24; ROADMAP; AGENTS.md rules.
Evidence: mrms, goes-aws, gibs (reviewed); globe-libs; webgl-runtime; parallax (no review key); terrain; prototype-mrms; prototype-globe and prototype-goes (unreviewed).

Live re-check: GOES-East ACHAC object kept by the prototype (scan 03:26 UTC), read with netCDF4: longitude_of_projection_origin -75.0; nominal_satellite_subpoint_lon -75.2; HT standard_name geopotential_height_at_cloud_top; HT units m; scale 0.3052037. No new network request.
inputs_corrections_applied: mrms.json review: 21.3 MB per step is a 2-hour window; whole days are 19.8-24.9 MB per step (594-746 MB per hour). Latest whole-CONUS 33-level gz step 20.0 MB (measured).
mrms.json review: latency 35-99 s is one step; whole day 29-120 s. MESH is 16-bit in the 2025 file, 8-bit in 2026.
mrms.json review refutes README section 4's 'MRMS carries its own no-coverage mask': no mask product exists. -999 and -99 both mean 'no radar data' (meanings unverified).
MRMS cells are 1.112 km N-S by 0.758 km E-W at 47 N (0.01 deg grid), not 1 km squares (README section 3).

parallax.json assumes GOES-East -75.2; the live re-read confirms -75.0 as the grid origin (prototype-goes.json). The Missoula 15 km shift changes by 0.171 km, so 'about 20 to 33 km' reads about 20 to 34 km.
goes-aws.json review: ACHAC is 10 km (300 x 500, 0.32 MB per step); ACHA2KMC is a separate 2 km product (1500 x 2500, 4.4-4.5 MB per step, from 2023-03-24). COD caps at 16.0.
gibs.json review: served layers TM7 (GeoColor) and TM6 (Band 13); late frames 76-96 min after label; a 404 can later return 200; off-grid times return the previous frame or 404.

a.name: Draped satellite texture (GOES GeoColor, Band 13)
a.data_needed: GIBS WMTS GOES-East/West GeoColor (1 km at sub-point) and Band 13 (2 km native), 10-min frames, valid times labelled. Alternative: Python-made PNG from ABI CMIPC C13 (2 km).
a.computed_where: Python picks frame, valid time and freshness. Browser fetches fixed-region tiles and draws them.
a.bytes: GIBS 2 x 2 Montana box: 0.28-0.42 MB per layer per 10-min frame (gibs.json, measured); 1.7-2.5 MB per hour and 3.4-5.0 MB per 2 h loop (computed). Python C13 PNG, 0.02 deg, plan box: 128.8 KB per 5-min frame (prototype-goes.json, unreviewed); 1.5 MB per hour (computed).
a.gpu_class: low: 4 tiles of 256 px RGBA = 1.05 MB GPU per layer (computed); no 3D texture.
a.represents: Satellite image of cloud tops (observation). Clouds sit where the ground grid puts them, not corrected for cloud-top height. No cloud base. GeoColor is a colour composite, not a height or a radar estimate.
a.legend: Satellite image (GOES, observation). Not corrected for cloud-top height. The cloud top is drawn where the satellite's ground grid puts it, away from the satellite (north-west or north-east of Montana): about 3 to 4 km off for a 2 km top, about 20 to 33 km off for a 12 to 15 km top (parallax.json wording; see inputs_corrections_applied). Cloud base is not observed. Valid and retrieved times shown.
failures: Parallax: uncorrected (see common_failure_modes).
Late frames 76-96 min after label; a 404 can later return 200; off-grid times return the previous frame or 404 (gibs.json). Show a gap, never the previous frame.
The 15-min GOES limit is a proposal; the prototype run showed 32-42 min old (prototype-globe.json).
A blank tile is Unavailable, not sky.
a.libraries: Cesium WMTS time dimension and UrlTemplateImageryProvider (globe-libs.json, wave 1 raw HTML). deck.gl TileLayer experimental on GlobeView (re-checked). MapLibre 5.0.0+ globe with raster tiles (re-checked). globe.gl globeTileEngineUrl (globe-libs.json).
a.phase_fit: Phase 1 default GOES drape; Phase 4 time loop.

b.name: Cloud deck lifted by cloud-top height (mesh vertex displacement)
b.data_needed: ACHA cloud-top height with DQF. Only DQF 0 carries a valid height in every ACHAC scene checked (goes-aws.json; prototype-goes.json). ACHAC 10 km: 0.32 MB per 5-min file. ACHA2KMC 2 km: 4.4-4.5 MB per step (not opened by the prototypes). Imagery as (a).
b.computed_where: Python: DQF filter, native-cell extraction, per-cell displacement table from the parallax geometry, height packing. Browser: vertex shader lifts each native cell and samples the image at the apparent point, not the ground point.
b.bytes: Native heights, uint16, per frame: ACHAC 1,777 review-box cells = 3.6 KB (goes-aws.json; 2 B x cells) plus 1.8 KB DQF. 2 km grid, 44,363 review-box cells = 88.7 KB (goes-aws.json). Plan box, unreviewed: ACHAC 2,647 native cells = 5.3 KB; 0.02 deg PNG = 17.2 KB east, 20.1 KB west (prototype-goes.json). Per hour (12 frames): 43 KB at 10 km; 1.06 MB at 2 km (computed). Static shift table once: 14 KB or 355 KB (computed, 2 x float32 per cell).
b.gpu_class: low at 10 km (1,777 vertices, 3,554 triangles, computed); medium at 2 km (44,363 vertices, 88,726 triangles, plus a texture fetch per vertex, computed).
b.represents: The top surface of the highest cloud at an estimated height (a satellite retrieval, not a measurement). The height is geopotential, referenced to the geoid, about sea level, not the ground (CF standard name; prototype-goes.json). No cloud base. Cells without a valid height show as No height, never as ground.
b.legend: Corrected for cloud-top height. The height is a satellite estimate; an error of 1 km in it moves the cloud by about 2 km (parallax.json wording). Cloud base is not observed. Grey = no valid height.
failures: Texture coordinate must be the apparent point Q(G,h) from parallax.json's method; sampling the image at the ground point G shows the wrong cloud.

Resampling to a finer grid adds false detail: 10 km pixels are 24.4 x 10.9 km (GOES-East) and 21.3 x 10.8 km (GOES-West) at the box centre; 2 km pixels 4.9 x 2.2 km (prototype-goes.json, unreviewed). Draw native footprints.

Valid heights are sparse: 41.2% of review-box 10 km cells (733 of 1,777, 01:41; goes-aws.json); 48.0% of plan-box native cells (1,270 of 2,647, 03:28; unreviewed). The 2 km DQF-0 share is not measured; the 2 km scene at 00:01 had 13,125 review-box cells with a height (goes-aws.json; DQF split not given).
Unexplained: median valid height 11.2 km with median band-13 brightness 269.6 K (warm for high tops), r = -0.62 (goes-aws.json). Needs a recorded high-top case before Phase 2 acceptance.
A per-cell linear model at 12 km reproduces parallax.json rows at 2-15 km within 0.042 km (computed; 4 sites, 2 satellites).
b.libraries: three.js 0.186.1: custom BufferGeometry and ShaderMaterial (WebGL2 only since r163). MapLibre 6.14: custom layer gets a WebGL2 context (typings). Cesium: CustomShader documented for Model, 3D Tiles and VoxelPrimitive (globe-libs.json); a displaced ground mesh needs a Model or custom primitive (unverified). deck.gl: custom layer on experimental GlobeView.

c.name: Volumetric ray-marching in a 3D texture (dense 33-level MRMS crop)
c.data_needed: MRMS MergedReflectivityQC, 33 levels (heightAboveSea 500-19,000 m), 2-min steps (mrms.json). Python crop of 1350 x 615 per level, with a class code per cell (20/35/50 dBZ) and a separate no-data code.
c.computed_where: Python: decode, crop, class coding, packing to one 3D array. Browser: upload the texture, march rays, map class code to colour and opacity from a fixed legend table (drawing only). No browser thresholds, no interpolation.
c.bytes: Dense array per frame = 1350 x 615 x 33 texels: uint8 27.40 MB; uint16 54.80 MB (computed). Per hour (30 frames): 822 MB uint8. Per 2 h loop (60 frames): 1,644 MB uint8. The whole-CONUS 33-level gz step is 20.0 MB (mrms.json, measured), so one uncompressed crop is larger than a full source step. gzip of the array not measured.
c.gpu_class: high. 27.4 M texels (27 MB GPU at R8). Fit: each axis at most MAX_3D_TEXTURE_SIZE 2048 (webgl-runtime.json, SwiftShader): the plan box fits one texture; the CONUS grid 7000 x 3500 does not. Fetch load: 900 x 720 canvas x 33 samples = 21.4 M per frame = 1.28 G per second at 60 fps (computed). Integrated GPUs not measured.
c.represents: Radar echo strength per height level, above sea level. No value between levels. No echo above threshold is not clear. -99 and -999 both mean no radar data (meaning unverified).
c.legend: Radar echo strength (dBZ), MRMS 3D mosaic. Heights are above sea level, not above ground. Grey = no radar data, not clear. Estimate from radar, not observed hail or damage.
failures: Trilinear sampling across levels 0.25-1 km apart creates values never measured. Sample the nearest level only.
Levels below ground: Billings sits at 952 m (terrain.json), so the 0.5 and 0.75 km levels are below ground and 1.0 km is 48 m above. Clip to the terrain. Montana-wide share not computed.
Beam overshoot far from the four Montana radars (D24) leaves low levels empty: label as no radar data.
A partial frame (03:08:36 run lacked 16-19 km; prototype-mrms.json) must show a gap, not zeros.
Cells are 1.11 km x 0.76 km, not square.
c.libraries: three.js Data3DTexture (MIT; re-checked in doc and tarball). Cesium VoxelPrimitive (Apache-2.0): experimental (doc re-checked); WebGL2 since 1.134 (CHANGES.md line 390); Texture3D since 1.138 (CHANGES.md line 299). deck.gl: setTexture3DData but no VolumeLayer (bundle, 0 matches). MapLibre 6.14: no volume API (typings, re-checked). globe.gl: none.
c.phase_fit: Phase 3 experiment only, behind a default-off setting and a measured test on the D-G7 floor.

d.name: Sparse voxels or boxes (what the prototype draws)
d.data_needed: The same 33-level MRMS step; an output list [i,j,k,dbz] of valid cells at or above a threshold (mrms_volume.py v0.1; k = index in levels_km).
d.computed_where: Python: inclusive threshold, crop, index, height-true positions. Browser: instanced boxes or points (drawing only).
d.bytes: Measured JSON, uncompressed, about 16.7 B per voxel. Per frame at the event peak: 20 dBZ 10.33 MB; 35 dBZ 1.67 MB; 50 dBZ 0.23 MB. Quiet frame 9.6 KB. Per hour: 310 / 50 / 7 MB; per 2 h loop: 620 / 100 / 14 MB. Upper bounds, since every frame is taken at the peak sample. Packed binary at 5 B per voxel (computed, not built): 3.10 / 0.50 / 0.07 MB per frame.
d.gpu_class: 20 dBZ high: 619,321 instances; typed arrays about 8.1 MB at 13 B per voxel (computed). Cesium add and remove rewrite the vertex buffer (O(n)), so per-frame rewrites are costly (PointPrimitiveCollection doc). 35 dBZ medium: 99,854 instances, 1.3 MB. 50 dBZ low: 13,482 instances, 0.18 MB.
d.represents: Each box is a radar estimate of one cell at one height. The JSON carries counts and voxels only, so no per-cell no-data mask exists (prototype-mrms.json limitation). Gaps look like clear air unless a mask layer is added.
d.legend: Radar echo strength at or above 35 dBZ (MRMS, estimate; not hail, not damage). Boxes sit at their height above sea level. Grey = no radar data, not clear.
failures: No per-cell no-data mask: a missing box reads as clear air.
Sub-terrain boxes must be clipped to the terrain.
The 20 dBZ peak frame is 10.3 MB; a per-frame budget (README section 10, not yet written) is needed before it ships.
A missing level is a gap; never copy the previous frame.
Server decode of a 33-level frame: 21-23 s and 409 MB peak RSS (prototype-mrms.json, sandbox).
d.libraries: Cesium PointPrimitiveCollection (doc re-checked: 'prefer a few collections, each with many points') and Primitive batching (wave 1 raw HTML). three.js InstancedMesh and deck.gl ScatterplotLayer are standard but not re-checked (unverified).
d.phase_fit: Phase 3 first candidate at 50 and 35 dBZ; 20 dBZ only if the budget allows.

e.name: Isosurfaces: mesh in Python, glTF or 3D Tiles in the browser, at 20 / 35 / 50 dBZ
e.data_needed: The same voxel field; a mesher inside the publish job (not chosen or checked here).
e.computed_where: Python entirely; the browser loads the mesh.
e.bytes: Not measured. Proxy from stored voxel faces (computed): exposed interior faces x 2 triangles x 72 B (non-indexed positions and normals). 20 dBZ: 359,134 faces, 718,268 triangles, 51.7 MB per frame (1,551 MB per hour). 35 dBZ: 80,145 faces, 160,290 triangles, 11.5 MB (346 MB per hour). 50 dBZ: 14,996 faces, 29,992 triangles, 2.16 MB (65 MB per hour). Versus measured voxel JSON: 5.0x, 6.9x, 9.3x. Indexed glTF would be smaller (not measured). Level spacing is uneven, so vertical faces are not physical areas.
e.gpu_class: high at 20 dBZ (718k-triangle proxy); medium at 35 dBZ (160k); low at 50 dBZ (30k).
e.represents: A threshold surface. Marching cubes (standard method, not checked here) places the surface by linear interpolation along cell edges, so positions fall between measurements (false precision). A face-based surface avoids that and is heavier.
e.legend: Outline of radar echo at 35 dBZ (MRMS, estimate). Surface positions are estimated between grid cells. Not a probability shell.
failures: Interpolated surface positions: forbidden unless disclosed.
No-data boundaries would draw false edges if treated as no echo.
Box-edge faces cut surfaces (2,806 faces at 20 dBZ, computed).
Sub-terrain surfaces.
e.libraries: Cesium Model (glTF) and three.js GLTFLoader are standard, not re-checked. 3D Tiles route not checked (unverified).
e.phase_fit: Phase 3 after d proves the pipeline; 35 and 50 dBZ.

f.name: Stacked translucent slabs, one per level
f.data_needed: 33 per-level images per frame (PNG or raw).
f.computed_where: Python renders each level; the browser stacks textured quads.
f.bytes: Raw 8-bit: 830,250 B per level, 27.40 MB per frame (computed; equal to c). PNG per slab not measured. Per hour 822 MB; per 2 h loop 1,644 MB (computed).
f.gpu_class: high on memory and fill: RGBA8 slabs 109.6 MB GPU vs 27.4 MB for R8 (computed); 33 full-box quads = 21.4 M fragment writes per frame at 900 x 720 (computed).
f.represents: Discrete layers, one per height level. Stacking implies continuous vertical structure that was not measured.
f.legend: Each layer is one radar height level above sea level, not a continuous volume. Layers below ground are hidden.
failures: Implied vertical continuity (false precision).
Sub-terrain slabs appear inside the terrain.
Uneven spacing.
Translucent stacking muddies dBZ colours; opacity must not encode severity.
f.libraries: Generic textured quads in any listed library (not re-checked).
f.phase_fit: Not recommended for the main volume; possible as a Phase 3 level inspector.

g.name: 2D fallback drape: NWS radar WMS (layer 1, D7)
g.data_needed: NWS radar_base_reflectivity WMS (D7); prototype export 1280 x 583 px over the Montana box.
g.computed_where: NWS renders the PNG. Python decides valid time and freshness (the app does this already).
g.bytes: Blank Montana export 866 B (prototype-globe.json, unreviewed; URL not recorded, so not re-run). Echo-bearing export not measured (unverified). Cadence not measured.
g.gpu_class: low: one RGBA texture 1280 x 583 = 2.98 MB GPU (computed).
g.represents: 2D base reflectivity, one tilt, no height. Blank means no echo at check time or no coverage, never an all-clear (prototype-globe.json).
g.legend: NWS base reflectivity, 2D radar estimate. No height. Blank is not clear.
failures: A blank box read as clear.
Valid-time mismatch: the CONUS footprint covering Montana was 43-56 s older than the app's newest footprint (prototype-globe.json).
Single tilt, not a volume.
g.libraries: Cesium WebMapServiceImageryProvider, MapLibre raster WMS and globe.gl are not re-checked (unverified). The flat app already uses WMS through Folium (D7).
g.phase_fit: Phase 1 fallback; the flat map stays the reference.

techniques.h_considered_not_ranked: Server-side GPU rendering streamed to the window (the Purdue system used VNC remote rendering, see survey). It moves the GPU to a server: a second service, cost and privacy questions (D-G2), not measured here. Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles: paid per 1,000 events and cache-prohibited under the terms quoted in globe-libs.json; not a weather layer; out of scope.

phase_ranking.criteria: Ordered by honesty fit first (no interpolation, no false coverage), then measured bytes per frame, then GPU class. Ranks are not a verdict on quality.
phase_1_2d_globe: a: first. 0.28-0.42 MB per layer per frame; low GPU; legend discloses parallax.
g: fallback. Blank is not clear.
phase_2_cloud_lift: b at 2 km (ACHA2KMC): first for footprint (4.9 x 2.2 km vs 24 x 11 km) and native cells (44,363 vs 1,777 in the review box). Gate: measure the DQF-0 share in the box first.
b at 10 km (ACHAC): second. Smallest server file (0.32 MB per step) and smallest browser bytes (3.6 KB per frame); coarse.
a stays the default uncorrected layer.
phase_3_storm_volumes: d at 50 dBZ, then 35 dBZ: measured bytes, low to medium GPU, discrete boxes. Needs the no-data mask layer first.
e at 50 and 35 dBZ after d: smoother, but interpolated positions; proxy 2-12 MB per frame.
d at 20 dBZ only if the per-frame budget allows 10.3 MB at the peak.
c as a measured experiment only: high GPU, 27.4 MB per frame.
f as a level inspector only.
phase_ranking.phase_4_time_loop_upper_bound_per_2h_at_: a 3.4-5.0 MB per layer; b at 10 km 0.13 MB (native, computed); b at 2 km 2.1-3.2 MB (computed); d at 50 dBZ 14 MB; d at 35 dBZ 100 MB; e at 50 dBZ 130 MB (proxy); d at 20 dBZ 620 MB; e at 35 dBZ 692 MB (proxy); c 1,644 MB uint8; f 1,644 MB uint8 equivalent; e at 20 dBZ 3.1 GB (proxy). Ordered by bytes only.
phase_ranking.phase_5_laptop_gpu_class: low: a, g, b at 10 km, d at 50 dBZ. Low-medium: e at 50 dBZ. Medium: d at 35 dBZ, e at 35 dBZ, b at 2 km. High: d at 20 dBZ, e at 20 dBZ, c, f. Not timed; the D-G7 floor test is required before any ranking is treated as performance.

library_support.cesium_1.146.0: Apache-2.0; pinned with SRI in the prototype (prototype-globe.json). Viewer defaults: baseLayer ImageryLayer.fromWorldImagery(), baseLayerPicker true (doc re-checked); the bundle maps the default to an Ion asset (globe-libs.json), so set baseLayer and baseLayerPicker false. VoxelPrimitive experimental (doc re-checked); WebGL2 since 1.134; Texture3D since 1.138 (CHANGES.md). EllipsoidTerrainProvider: no height data (doc).
library_support.three_0.186.1: MIT. WebGL2 only since r163 (WebGLRenderer.js in tarball, re-checked). Data3DTexture: 'Creates a three-dimensional texture from raw data, with parameters to divide it into width, height, and depth.' (doc re-checked). No volume example in the package doc.
library_support.globe.gl_2.46.2: MIT. Wraps three-globe; needs three >= 0.179; no volume API (README, wave 1). bumpImageUrl is a bump map, not elevation.
library_support.deck.gl_9.4.0: MIT. GlobeView: 'This class is experimental' (doc re-checked); TileLayer on the globe is experimental (doc re-checked). setTexture3DData in the bundle; no VolumeLayer (re-checked).
library_support.maplibre_gl_6.14.0: BSD-3-Clause. 'Globe View or Globe Projection was released as part of MapLibre GL JS 5.0.0 in January 2025.' (roadmap page re-checked). Custom render gets a WebGL2 context (typings, re-checked). DEM 'terrarium' supported. No volume or 3D-texture API (re-checked).

quotes: Layering this volumetric data on top of 2D composite reflectivity
By isolating high reflectivity values in radar data, we were able to extract and visualize the storm's hail column.

quotes: Level II Data Processing: Parses raw NEXRAD binary data into volumetric voxel fields using ray marching shaders.
Renders radar volumes over a 3D USGS global map with elevation data and GIS boundaries.
viewer_survey.status: 'Name your own price'. Licence name not on the page. Source link given (github.com/Trancsfict8/NEXRAD_Spatial); a derivative of the open-source OpenStorm Radar project.

viewer_survey.viewer: Sundaram et al., Purdue: near real-time 3D NEXRAD Level II on TeraGrid (research system; date not on the pages read)

quotes: The data is visualized by a hardware-accelerated, texture-based volumetric renderer on a Graphics Processing Unit (GPU).
Customized transfer functions that map data values to optical properties such as color and opacity are provided to users
viewer_survey.status: Research paper; read from PDF pages 1-2 as page images.

viewer_survey.viewer: Windy 3D globe (negative control: flat maps on a globe; radar and satellite not in 3D, per a moderator)
viewer_survey.technique: Flat map layers placed on a globe; not a model of the atmosphere.
quotes: The 3D mode in Windy is not a three-dimensional image of the atmospheric layer.
Except very special data, Radar nor Satellite data are not available in three-dimension
viewer_survey.status: Forum moderator statement. The page shows a deletion notice; date not visible.

viewer_survey_note: Library, not a viewer: CesiumJS 1.138 volume rendering uses WebGL2 3D textures: 'Volumetric rendering with voxels in CesiumJS was optimized with WebGL2's 3D Textures for reduced memory usage at runtime.' (https://cesium.com/blog/2026/02/03/cesium-releases-in-february-2026/). No GOES or radar example was found on it.
negative_searches: No browser-based GOES 3D viewer, and no browser-based NEXRAD or MRMS 3D volume viewer, found in nine searches. Zoom Earth: no 3D globe description found (one search). NASA World Wind: reported discontinued in a 2019 Cesium post. Browser radar tools seen were 2D (netbymatt NEXRAD JavaScript tools; Tempest Radar per a package listing). Not opened.
legend_rules: Radar legends read 'Radar echo strength (dBZ)'. No severity colour ramps. Opacity encodes echo class only, never severity (supervisor product critic).
Every radar legend says: estimate from radar, not observed hail or damage; grey or blank is no radar data, not clear.
MRMS heights: 'above sea level'. ACHA heights: 'geopotential, about sea level', not above ground. Satellite cloud layers: 'cloud top only; cloud base not observed'.
Every layer shows valid time, retrieved time, age and Live, Stale or Unavailable (D12). The GOES and MRMS limits are proposals and need a DECISIONS entry before use.
No probability shells. 20, 35 and 50 dBZ are echo thresholds, labelled as such.
common_failure_modes: Sub-terrain MSL levels: Billings (952 m, terrain.json) has MRMS 0.5 and 0.75 km below ground. Montana-wide share unverified.

Parallax: uncorrected cloud tops are displaced about 3-4 km (2 km top) to about 20-34 km (12-15 km top). The 34 km end depends on the -75.0 origin (prototype-goes.json, unreviewed; live attribute re-read).
No-data cells: MRMS -999 and -99 both mean 'no radar data' (meanings unverified). There is no mask product, and the voxel JSON has no per-cell mask.
Frame gaps: 62 of 63 stamps common to all 33 levels today (mrms.json), about 1.6% of steps incomplete over 00:00-02:04. GIBS late frames 76-96 min. Show gaps, never the previous frame.

Interpolation (forbidden): trilinear sampling across levels, resampling 10 km pixels to 0.02 deg, and marching-cubes edge interpolation each create values between measurements. Send native cells with their footprints.
Coverage: beam overshoot far from the four Montana radars (supervisor log; D24) leaves low levels empty. No echo is not clear.
unverified: Meanings of MRMS -99 and -999 (NSSL table unreadable); MESH units (mm likely) and codes -1 and -3.
Montana-wide share of MRMS levels below ground (only Billings checked).
ACHA2KMC DQF-0 share in the Montana box; the 2 km DQF split at 00:01 (13,125 review-box cells with a height).
Mesh and isosurface triangle counts and sizes are proxies from voxel faces (computed); no mesher was run. gzip or Brotli size of any payload.
GPU timings and memory on any real GPU (SwiftShader only). Echo-bearing NWS WMS export size and cadence (only a blank 866 B export was reported).
